alex (Docs): Quick flag: the /v1/chat/generate reference shows temperature: 50 in the example curl and snippets. That looks percent-style (0-100) but our runtime uses a float 0.0-2.0. Customers are confused.

ben (API): Good catch. That was leftover from an older draft. Server still accepts legacy integers for a short window, but canonical is 0.0-2.0 and values >2.0 are clamped to 2.0. Docs should show a decimal example.

carmen (SDK): I'll update Python/JS examples to use temperature=0.5 and add a one-line migration helper comment: `# if you have percent values: temp = min(2.0, (pct/100.0)*2.0)`. Also update the JSON Schema to indicate number, minimum 0.0, maximum 2.0.

alex (Docs): Draft migration blurb: "Note: temperature is a float from 0.0 to 2.0. Older examples may show percent values (0-100). Convert by dividing by 100 and scaling to the 0-2 range or use the SDK helper." Short mapping snippet would help.

ben (API): We can add the mapping snippet and an explicit sentence about clamping. Backend team ok with brief note about accepting legacy ints for now.

carmen (SDK): PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2201 0 updates: fixed examples, updated snippets, added migration note and schema. Requesting review from @alex and @ben.

deploy-bot: docs-build: queued (job 9901)
deploy-bot: docs-build: succeeded (job 9901) preview: https://deploy-preview-2201--docs.redwood.ai/chat/generate

alex (Docs): Reviewed and left a tiny nit to show `response.choices[0].message.content` in the Python comment. Otherwise LGTM.

carmen (SDK): Pushed the small fix. CI green, merging now.

carmen (SDK): Filed infra ticket to add a docs linter catching percent-style temperatures (infra#900).

alex (Docs): Approved and merged. Adding a changelog blurb under "Docs updates". Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
